summary: Full brief on 241522065-1, a 505 ppm, 17.437 d dip on HIP 67102 (F7V, Tmag 8.3), promoted from the second list. I found no kill and no hold: the dip is real and periodic from 2021 to 2026 at the same depth in both product families, sits at the target in every sector's difference image, shows no secondary at any phase, and TRICERATOPS's pass rests on stars 33" to 37" out that the pixels exclude and on 0036's drop of an artifact that 2MASS and Gaia show is not a star. Notes for the maintainer: a 4 sigma Hipparcos-Gaia acceleration hints at an unseen companion that high-resolution imaging would test, and the star has a second candidate at 5.58 d (ours and eumemic's).

findings.claim: The second list's pixel pass rests on S99, a timing-suspect sector, but it does not need it: S65, the best sector vet-v3 keeps, gives 5.8", the transit's loss sits at the target in all five sectors, and every possible host is 4.3 or more standard errors from the mean fit; S64's 17.3" fit comes from half a transit that starts at a momentum dump.
findings.evidence: pixels.json (~/.cache/tess-hunt/drafts/m3-r2/241522065-1): offset_qual 2.33" from S99 (quality 0.90, QLP-era, timing-suspect); S102 4.2" (0.81), S101 17.3" (0.52), S65 5.8" (0.62), S64 17.3" (0.40); S38 was asked but has no image file and no no_image entry. Without the suspect sectors the best-quality sector is S65, 5.8" < 15", so the outcome does not change. /tmp/pixel-diag/summary_second.txt (the diagnosis's printout for the promoted rows, which 0033 says it did not discuss): 3x3-box z at the target against the z the light-curve depth predicts: S102 4.9/3.7, S101 5.2/5.5, S99 4.4/3.3, S65 9.4/8.0, S64 4.0/2.9; fit directions E/N: S102 -0.5/+4.2, S101 -10.1/-14.0, S99 +2.3/-0.3, S65 +3.1/-4.8, S64 -17.2/+1.6; quality-weighted mean E -2.6" N -2.0" (3.3" from the target), sky scatter 10.4". python3 /tmp/t13/241522065-1/pixmean.py (output pixmean.txt): the mean is 0.7 standard errors from the target and 34.3" (7.4 SE) from TIC 241522102 and 35.0" (7.6 SE) from TIC 241522037, the two stars that carry 93% of TRICERATOPS's NFPP (F2); on S64 and S65 alone, 4.3 and 4.6 SE. S64: . ~/.cache/tess-hunt/logs/m3-vars.sh; . ~/.cache/tess-hunt/logs/m3-rerun-vars.sh; cd ~/code/tess-hunt; /tmp/t13/heavy.sh uv run python /tmp/t13/241522065-1/ep43.py $VET2_RUN $SECOND2_RUN/tdi/241522065-1/tic241522065 (ep43.txt): S64 holds one transit, epoch 41 at BTJD 3055.338, inside a data gap 3055.082 to 3055.302 around momentum dumps at 3055.290 to 3055.295 (quality bit 32 in the tdi pickle), so its difference image holds only the post-dump half; its fit (SNRfit 8.1, westward) points at no likely host: the only star in that direction that neighbours.csv marks possible is Gaia DR3 6065889587552624128 (TIC 241522072) at 46.8", which needs a 72.7% eclipse. Inside 15": Gaia DR3 lists only G 19.6 at 7.97" and G 20.8 at 14.6" (neighbours.csv required_depth 9.59 and 23.65, so neither can host), and the TIC's one brighter row there is the ARTIFACT TRICERATOPS drops (F2). No TOI-1399.01-type host is visible; what remains is the usual unresolved zone within about 1" to 2" of the target, which high-resolution imaging would close. ExoFOP lists no imaging (literature.json search.exofop.imaging is empty).

findings.claim: TRICERATOPS's pass (mean NFPP 0.000148, FPP 0.0215) is carried by stars 33" and 37" out that the pixels exclude, no possible host sits in 0032's 20" to 25" band, and it leans on 0036's drop of ARTIFACT TIC 241522064 at 7.43", which the 2MASS flags and Gaia DR3 show is not a star.
findings.evidence: python3 /tmp/t13/241522065-1/tric.py ~/.cache/tess-hunt/drafts/m3-r2/241522065-1 (output tric.txt), from triceratops.json and probs.csv (the last of 10 runs): NFPP 1.53e-4, shared by TIC 241522102 (37.0", T 14.14, tdepth 0.123, 59%), TIC 241522037 (33.3", T 14.19, tdepth 0.138, 34%), TIC 241522032 (49.4", 5%) and TIC 241522126 (71.5", 2%). No kept star within 30" has tdepth > 0; the nearest kept star is 17.2" out (T 19.1). The Gaia stars at 19.5" and 23.8" need 115% and 102% (neighbours.csv), so 0032's band holds no possible host. TIC 241522097 (45.9", T 11.54, tdepth 0.022, the easiest host on depth) gets 1e-38: the TIC makes it a giant (R 15.1, d 2489 pc from Gaia plx 0.374 +- 0.035; cd ~/code/tess-hunt; uv run python /tmp/t13/241522065-1/tic_hosts.py, output tic_hosts.txt), so an eclipse on it would last far longer than the 4 h transit. FPP: TP 0.802, PTP 0.144, DTP 0.031, STP 0.022, SEB 3.8e-4, EB 2.4e-29, EBx2P 5.7e-13; contrast list empty. 0036: dropped_stars = ARTIFACT 241522064 and 7 DUPLICATEs whose originals are kept and sit 70" and farther out (/tmp/t13-dup/cone.csv). The ARTIFACT (cd ~/code/tess-hunt; uv run python /tmp/t13/241522065-1/artifact.py ~/.cache/tess-hunt/drafts/m3-r2/241522065-1/neighbours.csv, output artifact.txt, MAST TIC): 2MASS 13451195-5318306, 7.43" at PA 273 deg, Tmag 13.10, J 12.60, H 12.51, Ks 13.81, TWOMflag UUD-002-001-00c-0-0 (J and H not detected, rd_flg 0, so upper limits; Ks flagged c, confused by a bright neighbour's artifact; Ks fainter than J by 1.2 mag), no Gaia id. Gaia DR3's nearest source to that position is G 20.8 at 7.91", while Gaia does list a G 19.6 star 7.97" from the target, so it reaches far fainter than G about 13.5 at this separation. Had the row been a star, it would have needed only a 4.0% eclipse at 6.9" (summary_second.txt), inside the pixel rule's 15", and 0036's measurement expected it weighed (tdepth about 0.04, results/benchmarks/triceratops-tic-duplicates-2026-10-21.md line 114). 0036's limitations don't reach this result: the 12 SPLIT rows (66" to 194") all have tdepth 0, and the NFPP carriers are weighed with TIC parameters (tic_hosts.txt: 241522102 Teff 7228 R 1.63 M 1.62; 241522037 Teff 6421 R 1.81 M 1.29), not 2MASS estimates or solar defaults. 0032 (NFPP moves with the ephemeris): the run used the density-prior fit's ephemeris (t0 2340.4325, P 17.436716, duration 0.168 d; the search's t0 is 21 min later), and any move above 0.001 would land on stars the pixels exclude at 7 SE (F1). If SPOC's CROWDSAP (0.946 to 0.949) counted the artifact's 1.25% of the target's flux (cone.csv flux_vs_target 0.0125), the PDCSAP depth is over-corrected by at most about 1.3%, 0.6% in radius.

findings.claim: The Hipparcos-Gaia Catalog of Accelerations (EDR3 edition, an ADS hit) gives HIP 67102 a chi-square of 19.2, about a 4 sigma acceleration, so an unseen companion is likely despite RUWE 0.99; TRICERATOPS's priors don't condition on it, but even with a companion taken as certain the dip sits on the companion in only 13.5% of the bound-companion scenarios, and on an eclipsing binary in 0.3%.
findings.evidence: /tmp/t13/241522065-1/hgca.tsv (curl 'https://vizier.cds.unistra.fr/viz-bin/asu-tsv?-source=J/ApJS/254/42/catalog&HIP=67102&-out=HIP,Gaia,pmRA,e_pmRA,pmDE,e_pmDE,pmRAhg,e_pmRAhg,pmDEhg,e_pmDEhg,pmRAhip,pmDEhip,chi2'): Gaia EDR3 pm -20.197 +- 0.025, 18.565 +- 0.023 mas/yr against the Hipparcos-Gaia long-baseline pm -20.325 +- 0.024, 18.481 +- 0.029; chi2 19.21 (2 dof): p 6.7e-5, 3.99 sigma; 3 sigma is chi2 11.83 (cd ~/code/tess-hunt; uv run python /tmp/t13/241522065-1/hgca.py, output hgca.txt). The RA term alone is 3.7 sigma and Dec 2.3 sigma; the difference is about 72 m/s at the 10.14 mas parallax. Against it: Kervella et al. 2019 (DR2, also an ADS hit; /tmp/t13/241522065-1/kervella.tsv from J/A+A/623/A72/hipgpma) PMa S/N 0.97 (Hipparcos) and 0.82 (DR2), BinH 0, BinG2 0, dVt 58 +- 71 m/s. Gaia DR3 (/tmp/t13/241522065-1/gaia_dr3.csv, Gaia archive TAP): RUWE 0.990, ipd_frac_multi_peak 0, ipd_gof_harmonic_amplitude 0.021, non_single_star 0, RV 36.61 +- 0.15 km/s over 10 transits, rv_chisq_pvalue 0.79, rv_renormalised_gof -1.20, rv_amplitude_robust 0.94 km/s. Hipparcos (I/239) MultFlag empty, HvarType C; WDS (B/wds) has no entry within 2'. So: a possible companion of unknown mass and separation, with no sign of a close stellar one. From probs.csv (last run; tric.txt): PTP 0.1437 against STP 0.0219, SEB 3.8e-4, SEBx2P 4.8e-5, so the companion carries 0.135 of the bound-companion weight, almost all of it a planet on the companion (STP, 4.8 Re), and 0.0026 an eclipsing binary. The transit density agrees with the F7V TIC star (0.9 sigma), which argues against a small dense companion as host. Nothing here moves FPP toward 0.5. What would settle the companion: high-resolution imaging and an RV trend. Flagged in hits_flagged for the measurement, not for any claim in the text.

findings.claim: No secondary at any phase: LEO-Vetter's ModShift secondary (3.44 sigma at phase 0.028) fails all three of its own tests even without the red-noise scaling, a box scan finds nothing above the light curve's own spread, and odd/even, shape and density agree with a planet.
findings.evidence: $TRIAGE_RUN/evidence/241522065-1.json leo_flux.evidence.metrics (all 9 transits, 4 of them timing-suspect): sig_sec 3.442 at phs_sec 0.0282 (0.49 d after the primary), dep_sec 105 +- 30 ppm, sig_ter 2.731 (0.359), sig_pos 2.660 (0.335), sig_pri 18.83, Fred 1.362, FA1 5.090, FA2 2.689. LEO's rule (.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/leo_vetter/thresholds.py:170-189; criteria/triage-v1.toml MS4 0, MS5 -1, MS6 -1): MS4 = 3.442/1.362 - 5.090 = -2.56 (with Fred 1, -1.65); MS5 = 3.442 - 2.731 - 2.689 = -1.98; MS6 = 3.442 - 2.660 - 2.689 = -1.91. Unlike 370977908-1, it would stay unflagged without the red-noise scaling, and the secondary is only 0.71 sigma above the tertiary. . ~/.cache/tess-hunt/logs/m3-vars.sh; . ~/.cache/tess-hunt/logs/m3-rerun-vars.sh; cd ~/code/tess-hunt; /tmp/t13/heavy.sh uv run python /tmp/t13/241522065-1/scan.py $VET2_RUN (scan.txt), the light curve rebuilt as vet.py builds it, boxes of the density-prior duration 0.168 d: at the ModShift secondary's phase -30 +- 25 ppm (PDCSAP 38, 64, 65) and -53 +- 20 (all six sectors), both rises; phase 0.5 -1 +- 22 and 6 +- 20. Scan over phase 0.02 to 0.98 (PDCSAP): strongest dip 0.802, 103 +- 20 ppm (5.2 sigma white) from events +130, -85, +121, +157, +129 (/tmp/t13/241522065-1/phase802.py, phase802.txt), one of which (BTJD 3086.759) falls on a 5.58 d transit (F6); the scan's sd is 1.72 sigma and its strongest rise -4.9 sigma (phase 0.104), so it is red noise, and it is not in the six-sector top eight. The six-sector scan's dip at 0.358 and rise at 0.334 come from one S101 jump after its gap at 4107.04 to 4107.27 (+536 ppm at 4107.823, -760 at 4107.389), the same feature ModShift's tertiary and positive picked up. Odd/even: vet-v3 1.9 sigma (pdcsap) and 0.1 sigma (qlp) against max 3.0; LEO trapezoid odd 627 +- 26, even 557 +- 25 ppm (1.9 sigma); per event, white errors, -2.6 sigma on PDCSAP, driven by the partial epoch 43 (F5), -1.6 on all six. Shape: b 0.48 (flat-prior) and 0.73 (density-prior), Rp/Rs 0.022, grazing in 0% of samples; density 0.9 sigma from the TIC's; Rp 3.0 to 3.1 Re; TRICERATOPS EB 2.4e-29 and EBx2P 5.7e-13 (probs.csv).

findings.claim: Two of the five PDCSAP transits are partial and sit at momentum dumps (0031's partly covered transit), and one reads 155 ppm in the flattened box because of a pre-dump ramp; the clean PDCSAP transits and the four QLP transits agree, no sector dominates, and the QLP transits land where the PDCSAP-only fit predicts.

Epoch 42 has no flagged cadence within 0.33 d and its nearest dump is 3.4 d away. . ~/.cache/tess-hunt/logs/m3-vars.sh; . ~/.cache/tess-hunt/logs/m3-rerun-vars.sh; cd ~/code/tess-hunt; /tmp/t13/heavy.sh uv run python /tmp/t13/241522065-1/ep43raw.py $VET2_RUN (ep43raw.txt), unflattened PDCSAP against a line fit to -0.6 to -0.1 d: epoch 43 in transit -547 ppm (pre-ingress slope 1387 ppm/d), epoch 42 -619, so epoch 43's low box depth is the flattened baseline at the gap, not a missing transit. Clean PDCSAP (0, 1, 42) weighted 531 +- 29 ppm; QLP 572 +- 25: the families agree, so no sign of a QLP dilution problem. Events per sector: S38 2, S64 1 half, S65 2 (one partial), S99 2, S101 1, S102 1. Holdout is inconclusive (0 seasons testable, need 2; checks.json), but the QLP transits, 55 to 60 periods after the last PDCSAP one, sit at the times the PDCSAP-only density-prior fit predicts at full depth, which is what the evidence-only run's holdout pass (2 held-out seasons predicted) records. QLP's S99 to S104 timing error (medians under 10 min, 0022) is small against the 4 h box. sector_depth passes (pdcsap p 0.81; qlp p 0.86).

findings.claim: The star carries a second periodic dip at 5.581 d, found by the search (rank 2) and published by eumemic, at a period ratio of 3.124 that is no harmonic and no eclipsing-binary pair; if both are on the target this is a two-candidate system, which by itself lowers the false-positive odds.
findings.evidence: checks.json other_signals: rank 2, P 5.580849, t0 2339.0053, SDE 10.5, 127 ppm, period_ratio 0.3201. $SNAP3/raw/eumemic/results_public_candidates_allsky.csv row TIC241522065_P5.581: P 5.580837, depth 148 ppm, MES 8.9, 26 transits, Rp 1.72 Re, tier C (MES < 10), set 'neighbour<15"' with nearest_capable_arcsec 7.43 (the ARTIFACT of F2), centroid_offset_arcsec 14.2, FPP 0.043, NFPP 1.3e-5. The dossier lists it as eumemic-allsky f1d17f0, unmasked (0021). . ~/.cache/tess-hunt/logs/m3-vars.sh; . ~/.cache/tess-hunt/logs/m3-rerun-vars.sh; cd ~/code/tess-hunt; /tmp/t13/heavy.sh uv run python /tmp/t13/241522065-1/scan.py $VET2_RUN (scan.txt): at the search's ephemeris and 3 h box, 153 +- 14 ppm over 14 PDCSAP events (S38 147 +- 30, S64 116 +- 22, S65 192 +- 22) and 133 +- 12 over 23 events in six sectors; no 5.58 d event falls within one duration of a 17.44 d transit. 17.436716 / 5.580849 = 3.1244: not on vet-v3's harmonics, and an eclipsing binary's two eclipses share one period, so the two signals are not one binary's pair. Whether the 5.58 d dip is on the target was not tested here.

findings.claim: Not known as a planet: the only catalogue row at this period is ExoMiner's FFI row for the S38 TESS-SPOC TCE, ExoFOP held no TOI or CTOI, and none of the 15 ADS hits names the star as a planet host, binary or variable or reports a period; four dismissals need a reason the title doesn't give.
findings.evidence: $SNAP3/raw/ExoMiner-v2/vetting_catalog_FFI.csv row 241522065-1-S38: P 17.43766, MES 10.30, mean_score 0.811 +- 0.068, label PC, n_tois_in_tic 0. grep for 241522065, 6065889518833005312, HIP 67102 and HD 119555 over $SNAP3/raw (gz files included) finds only that row and eumemic's 5.58 d candidate (F6): nothing in TOI, CTOI, archive, VSX, Gaia-EB or TESS-EB. literature.json search.exofop (LIT3_RUN): status ok, tois, ctois, planets, imaging, files and comments all empty; I could not reread ExoFOP live (connection refused, three tries on 2026-10-21). VSX within 3' (VizieR B/vsx/vsx): four variables 133" to 176" out with periods 0.0775 to 0.467 d, none commensurate (17.4367 / 0.467423 = 37.30). arXiv, OpenAlex and Zenodo returned 0 for all six names; the ADS answer (15) is carried from 20261020T091938Z-vetting-literature-2315775-066c by LIT3's resume (from_run). Screened all 15: catalogues, surveys and calibration samples. Dismissed for reasons the title doesn't show: Kervella et al. 2019 (2019A&A...623A..72K): no proper-motion anomaly for this star (F3); McDonald et al. 2012 (2012MNRAS.427..343M): no infrared excess, EIR 1.036, W4 ratio 1.059 (VizieR J/MNRAS/427/343, HIP 67102); de Geus 1990 Walraven photometry of southern OB associations (1990A&AS...85..915D): the star is not a Sco-Cen member, its pmDec +18.6 mas/yr has the opposite sign to Sco-Cen's and its RV is 36.6 km/s, and Hipparcos rates it constant (HvarType C, Hpscat 0.019 mag); Ruiz-Dern et al. 2018 red clump calibration (2018A&A...609A.116R): the star is a dwarf (TIC logg 4.30, Gaia FLAME logg 4.25, R 1.30 to 1.34), so at most a calibration star. Heller et al. 2017 photon sails (2017AJ....154..115H) computes travel times to about 22,000 stars within about 300 light-years (arXiv 1704.03871 abstract), which is where a star at 98.6 pc comes in. Only the HGCA hit is flagged (F3).
